content.content:
Tilts-The-Jug: "There is, if the hands are careful enough. The Chapter takes from those who can bear the loss. It takes no more than that. A hand that breaks what it touches is no use to us, so I must see how yours work. Keeps-What-Floats stands on the dock just west of this door. He took a necklace of polished blue jaspers from a Lookout of ours, one of the Chapter, while that Lookout slept. He keeps it in a locked strongbox under the eaves north-west of the house. Bring the necklace back, so that the Lookout has it again. Do Keeps-What-Floats no harm. If he is hurt, there is no pay and no place with us. Here are three lockpicks. There are three ways open. You can open his strongbox with the picks, or you can take his key, which he may give for good talk or sell for coin. Sits-By-The-Water drinks with him on the dock. Ask her about his habits, because I will not tell them."
Objective completed: Speak to Tilts-The-Jug inside the house on Soulrest's dock, behind the door beside S'Tabi.
Journal entry (A Dry Hand in a Wet City): Tilts-The-Jug, who keeps the Night-Reed Chapter's desk, wants to see how I work, and she gave me three lockpicks. A dock thief, Keeps-What-Floats, took a necklace of blue jaspers from a sleeping Chapter Lookout and keeps it in a locked strongbox under the eaves north-west of the house. I'm to take it back without harming him, by opening the strongbox or by getting his key; Sits-By-The-Water, who drinks with him, can tell me his habits. Keeps-What-Floats stands on the dock just west of the door beside S'Tabi.
New objective: Take the Blue Jasper Necklace from Keeps-What-Floats's strongbox, or get his key from him (Speech 35, or 60 gold).
Added: Lockpick x3
Tilts-The-Jug has nothing more to say to you.

content.content:
Bent-Spine: "A merchant drowned in the deep water just south of the trapdoor you came down. His lockbox of pledges lies locked on the floor, where he went down. A pledge is a thing a client left with him against a loan. Three of his clients wait on the south bank of the deep water for a diver, and each says one thing in the box is theirs. I want the box emptied before they find one. Dive down, open it and take what is inside. What becomes of what you take is yours to say. I will not tell you whom to give it to. The Chapter takes from those who can bear the loss, and these pledges are other people's. Whoever holds them can sell them back, or can sell silence about them. Blackmail is no trade of ours, and I will not have a Lookout of mine in it. The lock is a Novice lock. Here are three lockpicks. Go up through the trapdoor, and the deep water lies just south of it."
Objective completed: Ask Bent-Spine about the work he has.

I'm to dive to the lockbox, pick its lock and take what is inside.

== A Dry Hand in a Wet City (completed)
- S'Tabi, the Khajiit trader on Soulrest's dock, told me that if I want quiet work I should ask for Tilts-The-Jug, who keeps the Night-Reed Chapter's desk in the house behind him. I'm to speak to her inside the house on Soulrest's dock, behind the door beside S'Tabi.
- Tilts-The-Jug, who keeps the Night-Reed Chapter's desk, wants to see how I work, and she gave me three lockpicks. A dock thief, Keeps-What-Floats, took a necklace of blue jaspers from a sleeping Chapter Lookout and keeps it in a locked strongbox under the eaves north-west of the house. I'm to take it back without harming him, by opening the strongbox or by getting his key; Sits-By-The-Water, who drinks with him, can tell me his habits. Keeps-What-Floats stands on the dock just west of the door beside S'Tabi.
- I took the Blue Jasper Necklace out of Keeps-What-Floats's strongbox. I'm to bring it to Tilts-The-Jug inside the house on Soulrest's dock, behind the door beside S'Tabi.
- I gave Tilts-The-Jug the Blue Jasper Necklace, and because Keeps-What-Floats came to no harm, she paid me a hundred gold. I'm to take the coast ship from Soulrest's dock, east of the house, to Lilmoth, then go down the trapdoor north of Pusbottom at the edge of the deep water to speak to Bent-Spine below. The ship lands at Lilmoth's dock, and Pusbottom lies west of that dock.
- I went down through the trapdoor north of Pusbottom to the Night-Reed Chapter under Lilmoth, and Bent-Spine, the Chapter's fence, took me in as a Lookout. Tilts-The-Jug had set me to take a stolen necklace back from Keeps-What-Floats without harming him, and what became of him is now part of how she and the Chapter think of me.
== The Drowned Lockbox (completed)
- Bent-Spine, the Night-Reed Chapter's fence, has work for me now that I am a Lookout. I'm to ask him about it, in the Night-Reed Chapter under Lilmoth, down the trapdoor north of Pusbottom.
- Bent-Spine told me that a merchant drowned in the deep water north of Pusbottom, just south of the trapdoor, and that his lockbox of pledges lies locked on the floor. He wants it emptied before the three clients on the south bank find a diver, and he leaves to me what becomes of what is in it. He gave me three lockpicks. I'm to dive to the lockbox, pick its lock and take what is inside.
- I opened the drowned merchant's lockbox and found a worn bone figurine, a Neesak charm in a new silver mount and Kothringi glass beads. On the south bank, Neeta-Haj says the figurine was carved for her clutch, Okan-Tei says the charm was only pledged and Dar-Zeel says the beads are old family work. But the figurine is far older than any clutch of hers, a pledged charm would not have new silver on it, and the beads are cairn glass. I'm to choose: give all three to one client for a hundred and twenty gold, which leaves the other two with nothing, or sell each client back the thing they claim, which ends their lies.
- Neeta-Haj said the bone figurine was carved for her clutch, but it is worn smooth, far older than any clutch of hers. She would not own it at my word, and haggled; she bought it back for twenty gold, half its fair price. I'm to sell Okan-Tei the Newly Mounted Neesak Charm he claims, on the south bank.
- Okan-Tei said the charm was only pledged, but no one sets a pledge in a new silver mount. He haggled, and bought it back for forty-five gold, half its fair price. I'm to sell Dar-Zeel the Kothringi Glass Beads he claims, on the south bank.
- Dar-Zeel said the beads were old family work, but they are Kothringi glass of the kind the old cairns hold. He haggled, and bought them back for thirty gold. Neeta-Haj, Okan-Tei and Dar-Zeel each bought back the pledge they had lied about, so each has their own again and none was ruined. None of them is pleased with me, because I showed each of them to be a liar, but I sold no one's silence.

input.command: /tmp/ptb-17rjaz_m/play end --take 'Short and easy to follow. The quest givers named exactly where to go, and the travel command meant I never had to navigate. I understood the Night-Reed Chapter: thieves who take only from those who can bear the loss and harm no one. The lockbox job was the best part. It was a small moral puzzle: sell the pledges back, give all three to one client, or something worse. I picked the fair-price route, and it ended with all three clients owning their lies.
